reviews.text: I was looking for a good pet shop in the area for my pet. I loved the service at reception and from the lady who groomed and bathed my four-legged son. I will always take him there now.

I preferred to write here instead of personally communicating my first experience at the PetShop to the owners so that customers can have the opportunity to verify if what I observed has been corrected, or even if it was just an isolated case. I went to this PetShop for the first time this week because it's difficult in the region to find a place with glass doors to watch the bathing process; this was the factor that led me to the PetShop and also its 4.9 rating on Google.
My two short-haired chihuahuas went to get a bath, and I brought my shampoo and conditioner. I waited the entire time at the PetShop.
I noticed that the dogs are vulnerable to the possibility of going out onto the street, as the employees often leave both doors open at the same time, the door to the bathing area and the door that gives access to the street.
The glass door that gives access to the street needs to be a door that actually closes, and it's faulty and doesn't close on its own if they forget to open it. I noticed that the employees were passing through the doors without closing them, and animals are unpredictable; such carelessness can lead to the loss of an animal.
This safety issue caught my attention.
Another point I didn't like is that when I observed the rinsing of my second chihuahua, its ears weren't protected with cotton or anything like that. The pet shops I was used to protected the ear piercings to prevent water from entering the ears.
I started being attended to 10 to 15 minutes after my scheduled time, everything was fine, no problem. However, a woman who also came for the first time with her chihuahua had scheduled the same time as me and had been waiting for 45 minutes for her chihuahua's bath to begin. She was already discouraged from bringing her chihuahua back, and we both observed what I'm describing here.

When I got home, the bag with the shampoo was dirty. I noticed that the shampoo bottle cap had been opened and not screwed all the way in, causing it to leak. The shampoo cost over 200 reais, but it was almost empty, which is fine. However, if it had been new, I would have gone back to complain. I left a toothbrush and toothpaste for my dog; I returned the brush clean, and at home I saw that they hadn't rinsed the bristles. This is something simple, but it shows a lack of attention to the materials brought by the customer. So I think, if the materials are being delivered like this, that reinforces my advice to never leave my dogs in unfamiliar places. To clarify, they didn't mistreat my animals, that's not the case, but I've been to more careful places in other cities where I've lived.

One thing to improve is asking if the customer wants their pet decorated. I don't mind decorations, but I was used to being asked, and many times I asked them to just put stickers on the tips of their ears, which saves the pet shop materials.

Another area for improvement would be the car used to transport the pets. On the day I went, it was a black Volkswagen Gol with tinted windows, making it impossible to see inside. A car without tinted windows and with identification/advertising stickers for the pet shop would make the car less attractive for theft and offer transparency regarding the transport service and how the animals are being handled.

I don't intend to return at the moment because the doors were constantly open at the same time without anyone paying attention, I didn't see the ear protection, and I saw the other woman waiting 45 minutes to start hers. As someone with four short-haired dogs, I don't intend to return because I risk spending almost an hour waiting for a bath, like the woman mentioned, plus the time spent bathing one dog at a time, as happened with the two Chihuahuas I scheduled appointments for.

Attached is a photo of the door leading to the street, showing how it was constantly open during my time at the pet shop.

I hope to contribute some possible improvements to the pet shop.

Ms. Yasmin, your mother had already given her assessment, which was insensitive because she wanted us to rush the grooming of a 14-year-old pet, as she was in a hurry! We are available to discuss the lack of common sense that you showed. We also want to discuss the groomer, who you yourself said has been taking Mel to groomers for 10 years at other establishments. We cannot understand why you want to blame the establishment when the groomer is your choice, even though the fault is not hers either, as she did what needed to be done in a timely manner, considering the pet's age.

I scheduled my pet's bath and grooming for 1 PM.

However, upon arriving at 2:30 PM, the time I should have picked her up, the procedure (bathing) was still in progress.

When I inquired about the situation at the counter, I was informed that scissor grooming takes longer. However, I've had my pet for 14 years and known the groomer for about 10 years, and there has never been a delay of this nature before. When I expressed my dissatisfaction, I was treated unprofessionally and inappropriately, including being misused with the term "love," which I considered disrespectful.

I requested information about those responsible for the place and was given some names. Later, I received a message from the owner, who showed no interest in resolving the situation and maintained the same position, without showing any concern for what had happened.

I left the place after 3 PM, with a very negative experience marked by delays and lack of organization. I do not recommend it.

I would like to emphasize that the professional who takes care of my pet has always been attentive and works professionally, which is why I continue to trust her work.
